1 | """
2 | runner.py — replays a .wal script against the target site.
3 |
4 | This is the execution surface BotMedic observes. It is deliberately a real
5 | browser run rather than a text check: a patch is only trustworthy if the bot
6 | actually reaches the end of its script with the new selector in place.
7 |
8 | Supported WAL commands: webStart, webNavigate, webSet, webClick, webWait,
9 | webSelect, webAssert, webHover, webGet, webClose. Anything else is skipped,
10 | the same way an unrelated statement would be irrelevant to a selector break.
11 | """
12 |
13 | import json
14 | import re
15 | import time
16 | from pathlib import Path
17 | from typing import Optional
18 |
19 | from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright
20 |
21 | from fingerprint import DESCRIBE_JS, collect_candidates
22 | from parser import parse_wal
23 | from serve import BREAK_KEYS as SERVER_BREAK_KEYS, write_break_state
24 |
25 | PROJECT_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
26 | SNAPSHOT_DIR = PROJECT_ROOT / "snapshots"
27 |
28 | # The target site keeps one localStorage key per break, holding the string
29 | # 'true' or 'false'. That format belongs to the target app, not to us — the
30 | # engine writes what the site reads.
31 | BREAK_KEYS = (
32 | "break_login_id",
33 | "break_login_move",
34 | "break_login_text",
35 | "break_export_id",
36 | )
37 | DEFAULT_STEP_TIMEOUT_MS = 4000
38 |
39 |
40 | def _timeout_ms(step, default=DEFAULT_STEP_TIMEOUT_MS) -> int:
41 | """Convert a WAL ``--timeout "00:00:05"`` argument to milliseconds."""
42 | raw = step.args.get("timeout")
43 | if not raw:
44 | return default
45 | try:
46 | hours, minutes, seconds = (int(part) for part in raw.split(":"))
47 | total = (hours * 3600 + minutes * 60 + seconds) * 1000
48 | return total or default
49 | except ValueError:
50 | return default
51 |
52 |
53 | def _break_script(breaks: dict) -> str:
54 | """
55 | Build an init script that puts the break flags where the site looks.
56 |
57 | Every known key is written on every run, so a break switched off in one run
58 | is actually cleared rather than left over from the last one.
59 | """
60 | breaks = breaks or {}
61 | sets = "".join(
62 | f"localStorage.setItem({json.dumps(key)}, "
63 | f"{json.dumps('true' if breaks.get(key) else 'false')});"
64 | for key in BREAK_KEYS
65 | )
66 | return f"try {{ {sets} }} catch (e) {{}}"
67 |
68 |
69 | def apply_breaks(breaks: dict) -> None:
70 | """
71 | Write break flags to the server-side state file AND localStorage script.
72 | This ensures every browser — including IBM RPA Studio's isolated Chrome —
73 | sees the same DOM mutations on the next page load.
74 | """
75 | try:
76 | from serve import write_break_state
77 | write_break_state(breaks or {})
78 | except Exception:
79 | pass
80 |

82 | def _save_snapshot(page, run_id: str, base_url: str) -> str:
83 | """
84 | Save the current DOM to snapshots/<run_id>.html.
85 |
86 | Two things are done to the serialised DOM, and both matter:
87 |
88 | * a <base> tag is injected, so the snapshot still resolves the site's own
89 | stylesheet when it is re-opened for scoring — geometry signals are
90 | worthless against an unstyled page;
91 | * <script> blocks are removed. The snapshot is a record of the DOM at the
92 | moment the bot failed, and the target app builds its buttons at runtime:
93 | leaving the scripts in would let a re-opened snapshot rebuild itself into
94 | the healthy page and quietly erase the very break being diagnosed.
95 | """
96 | SNAPSHOT_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
97 | html = page.content()
98 | html = re.sub(r"<script[\s\S]*?</script>", "", html, flags=re.IGNORECASE)
99 | base_tag = f'<base href="{base_url}">'
100 | if "<head>" in html:
101 | html = html.replace("<head>", "<head>" + base_tag, 1)
102 | else:
103 | html = base_tag + html
104 |
105 | path = SNAPSHOT_DIR / f"{run_id}.html"
106 | path.write_text(html, encoding="utf-8")
107 | return str(path.relative_to(PROJECT_ROOT)).replace("\\", "/")

110 | def _execute_step(page, step, timeout: int):
111 | """Run one WAL step. Raises PlaywrightError when the element is missing."""
112 | command = step.command
113 | selector = step.selector_value
114 |
115 | if command == "webnavigate":
116 | page.goto(step.args.get("url", ""), wait_until="domcontentloaded")
117 | page.wait_for_timeout(120)
118 | return
119 |
120 | if command in ("webstart", "webclose"):
121 | return
122 |
123 | locator = page.locator(selector).first
124 |
125 | if command == "webset":
126 | locator.wait_for(state="visible", timeout=timeout)
127 | locator.fill(step.args.get("value", ""))
128 | elif command == "webclick":
129 | locator.wait_for(state="visible", timeout=timeout)
130 | locator.click()
131 | page.wait_for_timeout(200)
132 | elif command in ("webwait", "webwaitelement", "webassert"):
133 | locator.wait_for(state="visible", timeout=timeout)
134 | elif command == "webhover":
135 | locator.wait_for(state="visible", timeout=timeout)
136 | locator.hover()
137 | elif command == "webselect":
138 | locator.wait_for(state="visible", timeout=timeout)
139 | locator.select_option(step.args.get("value", ""))
140 | elif command == "webget":
141 | locator.wait_for(state="visible", timeout=timeout)
142 | locator.inner_text()
143 |

145 | def _classify_error(error: Exception) -> str:
146 | """Map a Playwright failure onto the error vocabulary the dashboard shows."""
147 | message = str(error).lower()
148 | if "timeout" in message and "waiting for" in message:
149 | return "ElementNotFound"
150 | if "strict mode violation" in message:
151 | return "AmbiguousSelector"
152 | if "not visible" in message or "hidden" in message:
153 | return "ElementNotVisible"
154 | if "net::" in message or "navigation" in message:
155 | return "NavigationFailed"
156 | return "ElementNotFound"

159 | def run_wal(
160 | wal_path: str,
161 | run_id: str,
162 | *,
163 | breaks: Optional[dict] = None,
164 | step_names: Optional[dict] = None,
165 | capture_fingerprints: bool = False,
166 | base_url: str = "http://127.0.0.1:8000",
167 | headless: bool = True,
168 | ) -> dict:
169 | """
170 | Replay a .wal script end to end.
171 |
172 | Args:
173 | wal_path: Script to run.
174 | run_id: Identifier used to name the DOM snapshot.
175 | breaks: Break flags to inject into the target site.
176 | step_names: Map of ordinal step key -> human step id.
177 | capture_fingerprints: Record an element fingerprint per selector step.
178 | Only meaningful on a run expected to succeed.
179 | base_url: Site origin, injected into saved snapshots.
180 | headless: Run the browser without a window.
181 |
182 | Returns:
183 | {
184 | "success": bool,
185 | "steps": [ {step_key, step_id, line_number, command, selector, ok, error} ],
186 | "failed_step": step dict or None,
187 | "fingerprints": {step_id: fingerprint},
188 | "snapshot": "snapshots/<run_id>.html" or None,
189 | "duration_sec": float,
190 | }
191 | """
192 | step_names = step_names or {}
193 | steps = parse_wal(wal_path)
194 | started = time.time()
195 |
196 | # The site server injects break state from disk into every page it serves.
197 | # Only overwrite the state file when breaks are explicitly provided — do NOT
198 | # clear it when breaks={}, so a break set from the panel stays active.
199 | if breaks:
200 | write_break_state(breaks)
201 |
202 | results = []
203 | fingerprints = {}
204 | failed_step = None
205 | snapshot_ref = None
206 |
207 | with sync_playwright() as playwright:
208 | browser = playwright.chromium.launch(headless=headless)
209 | context = browser.new_context()
210 | # Always sync localStorage from the server-side state file,
211 | # not from the breaks parameter — so the panel and the runner agree.
212 | from serve import read_break_state
213 | context.add_init_script(_break_script(read_break_state()))
214 | page = context.new_page()
215 |
216 | for step in steps:
217 | step_id = step_names.get(step.step_key, step.step_key)
218 | record = {
219 | "step_key": step.step_key,
220 | "step_id": step_id,
221 | "line_number": step.line_number,
222 | "command": step.command,
223 | "selector": step.selector_value,
224 | "ok": True,
225 | "error": None,
226 | }
227 |
228 | try:
229 | # The fingerprint is taken before the step runs: a click can
230 | # navigate away, and the element must be described as the bot
231 | # found it.
232 | if capture_fingerprints and step.has_selector:
233 | locator = page.locator(step.selector_value).first
234 | locator.wait_for(state="visible", timeout=_timeout_ms(step))
235 | described = locator.evaluate(DESCRIBE_JS)
236 | described.update({
237 | "step_id": step_id,
238 | "step_key": step.step_key,
239 | "selector": step.selector_value,
240 | "line_number": step.line_number,
241 | "url": page.url,
242 | })
243 | fingerprints[step_id] = described
244 |
245 | _execute_step(page, step, _timeout_ms(step))
246 | except Exception as error: # noqa: BLE001
247 | record["ok"] = False
248 | record["error"] = _classify_error(error)
249 | record["error_detail"] = str(error).split("\n")[0][:300]
250 | results.append(record)
251 | failed_step = record
252 | snapshot_ref = _save_snapshot(page, run_id, base_url)
253 | break
254 |
255 | results.append(record)
256 |
257 | if failed_step is None:
258 | # Green run: the snapshot is the reference the next break is scored against.
259 | snapshot_ref = _save_snapshot(page, run_id, base_url)
260 |
261 | browser.close()
262 |
263 | return {
264 | "success": failed_step is None,
265 | "steps": results,
266 | "failed_step": failed_step,
267 | "fingerprints": fingerprints,
268 | "snapshot": snapshot_ref,
269 | "duration_sec": round(time.time() - started, 2),
270 | }
271 |

273 | def count_matches(
274 | url: str,
275 | selectors: list[str],
276 | *,
277 | breaks: Optional[dict] = None,
278 | headless: bool = True,
279 | ) -> dict:
280 | """
281 | Count how many elements each selector matches on the page.
282 |
283 | A replacement selector that matches two elements is not a fix: the bot
284 | would click whichever came first and the failure would move somewhere
285 | harder to see.
286 | """
287 | counts = {}
288 | with sync_playwright() as playwright:
289 | browser = playwright.chromium.launch(headless=headless)
290 | context = browser.new_context()
291 | context.add_init_script(_break_script(breaks))
292 | page = context.new_page()
293 | page.goto(url, wait_until="domcontentloaded")
294 | page.wait_for_timeout(150)
295 | for selector in selectors:
296 | try:
297 | counts[selector] = page.locator(selector).count()
298 | except Exception: # noqa: BLE001 - an invalid selector counts as zero
299 | counts[selector] = 0
300 | browser.close()
301 | return counts
302 |

1 | """
2 | watcher.py — records green runs and reports broken ones.
3 |
4 | Two jobs, and the first one matters more than it looks:
5 |
6 | 1. On every **successful** run, fingerprint each element the bot touched and
7 | save a DOM snapshot. Without that record there is nothing to compare a
8 | broken page against, and the whole diagnosis is guesswork.
9 |
10 | 2. On a failed run, emit a FailureEvent in the frozen shape the engine reads.
11 | """
12 |
13 | import time
14 | from pathlib import Path
15 |
16 | from contracts import FailureEvent, read_json, write_json
17 | from registry import get_bot, step_names
18 | from runner import run_wal
19 | from serve import ensure_server
20 |
21 | PROJECT_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
22 | FINGERPRINT_DIR = PROJECT_ROOT / "fingerprints"
23 | INCIDENT_DIR = PROJECT_ROOT / "incidents"
24 |
25 |
26 | def new_run_id() -> str:
27 | """Allocate a run id of the form ``run-0042``."""
28 | INCIDENT_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
29 | existing = list(INCIDENT_DIR.glob("run-*.failure.json"))
30 | return f"run-{len(existing) + 1:04d}"
31 |
32 |
33 | def fingerprint_path(bot_id: str) -> Path:
34 | """Where a bot's fingerprint record lives."""
35 | return FINGERPRINT_DIR / f"{bot_id}.json"
36 |
37 |
38 | def load_fingerprints(bot_id: str) -> dict:
39 | """
40 | Load the fingerprints recorded on this bot's last green run.
41 |
42 | Returns:
43 | ``{step_id: fingerprint}``; empty when the bot has never run green.
44 | """
45 | stored = read_json(fingerprint_path(bot_id), default=None)
46 | return (stored or {}).get("steps", {})
47 |

49 | def record_baseline(bot_id: str, *, headless: bool = True) -> dict:
50 | """
51 | Run a bot against the healthy site and record what it touched.
52 |
53 | Returns:
54 | The run outcome from the runner, with ``fingerprint_file`` added.
55 | """
56 | bot = get_bot(bot_id)
57 | base_url = ensure_server()
58 | run_id = f"baseline-{bot_id}"
59 |
60 | outcome = run_wal(
61 | bot["wal_path"],
62 | run_id=run_id,
63 | breaks={},
64 | step_names=step_names(bot),
65 | capture_fingerprints=True,
66 | base_url=base_url,
67 | headless=headless,
68 | )
69 |
70 | if not outcome["success"]:
71 | failed = outcome["failed_step"] or {}
72 | raise RuntimeError(
73 | f"Baseline run for '{bot_id}' failed at step "
74 | f"{failed.get('step_id')} ({failed.get('error')}). "
75 | "Reset the target site in break.html and try again."
76 | )
77 |
78 | record = {
79 | "bot_id": bot_id,
80 | "bot_name": bot["bot_name"],
81 | "wal": bot["wal"],
82 | "risk_tier": bot["risk_tier"],
83 | "recorded_at": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z"),
84 | "green_snapshot": outcome["snapshot"],
85 | "duration_sec": outcome["duration_sec"],
86 | "steps": outcome["fingerprints"],
87 | }
88 | outcome["fingerprint_file"] = write_json(fingerprint_path(bot_id), record)

92 | def watch_run(bot_id: str, *, breaks: dict | None = None, headless: bool = True) -> dict:
93 | """
94 | Execute a bot and report what happened.
95 |
96 | Returns:
97 | ``{"run_id", "bot": bot, "outcome": run outcome, "failure": FailureEvent | None}``
98 | The failure event is also written to ``incidents/<run_id>.failure.json``.
99 | """
100 | bot = get_bot(bot_id)
101 | base_url = ensure_server()
102 | run_id = new_run_id()
103 |
104 | # Write break state to disk BEFORE running so every browser sees the same DOM
105 | if breaks:
106 | from runner import apply_breaks
107 | apply_breaks(breaks)
108 |
109 | outcome = run_wal(
110 | bot["wal_path"],
111 | run_id=run_id,
112 | breaks=breaks or {},
113 | step_names=step_names(bot),
114 | capture_fingerprints=outcome_should_fingerprint(breaks),
115 | base_url=base_url,
116 | headless=headless,
117 | )
118 |
119 | failure = None
120 | if not outcome["success"]:
121 | failed = outcome["failed_step"]
122 | failure = FailureEvent(
123 | run_id=run_id,
124 | bot_id=bot_id,
125 | risk_tier=bot["risk_tier"],
126 | failed_step=failed["step_id"],
127 | error=failed["error"],
128 | script_line=failed["line_number"],
129 | page_html_ref=outcome["snapshot"],
130 | )
131 | write_json(INCIDENT_DIR / f"{run_id}.failure.json", failure.to_dict())
132 | elif outcome["fingerprints"]:
133 | # A green run refreshes the baseline: today's healthy page is what
134 | # tomorrow's break gets compared against.

136 | record.update({
137 | "bot_id": bot_id,
138 | "bot_name": bot["bot_name"],
139 | "wal": bot["wal"],
140 | "risk_tier": bot["risk_tier"],
141 | "recorded_at": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z"),
142 | "green_snapshot": outcome["snapshot"],
143 | "steps": outcome["fingerprints"],
144 | })
145 | write_json(fingerprint_path(bot_id), record)
146 |
147 | return {"run_id": run_id, "bot": bot, "outcome": outcome, "failure": failure}
148 |

151 | """

153 |
154 | Recording against a page that is already broken would poison the baseline
155 | with the very state the engine is meant to detect.
156 | """
157 | return not any((breaks or {}).values())

1 | """
2 | parser.py — WAL script reader and patch writer for BotMedic.
3 |
4 | Reads an IBM RPA .wal script and returns every executable step with its line
5 | number, so the runner can replay the bot and the patcher can rewrite exactly
6 | one line without touching anything else.
7 |
8 | Step identity
9 | -------------
10 | A step is addressed by an ordinal key such as ``webclick#1`` — the first
11 | ``webClick`` in the file. Ordinals survive a selector patch, which is why they
12 | are used as the fingerprint key instead of the selector itself. The bot
13 | registry maps an ordinal key to a human step id (``login_submit``).
14 | """
15 |
16 | import os
17 | import re
18 | from dataclasses import dataclass, field
19 | from typing import Optional
20 |
21 | # Commands the runner knows how to replay.
22 | WEB_COMMANDS = {
23 | "webstart", "webnavigate", "webset", "webclick", "webget",
24 | "webwait", "webwaitelement", "webassert", "webhover", "webselect", "webclose",
25 | }
26 |
27 | # Commands that address an element and can therefore break.
28 | SELECTOR_COMMANDS = {
29 | "webset", "webclick", "webget", "webwait", "webwaitelement", "webassert",
30 | "webhover", "webselect",
31 | }
32 |
33 |
34 | @dataclass
35 | class WalStep:
36 | """A single executable line of a .wal script."""
37 |
38 | line_number: int
39 | command: str # lowercase: webclick, webset, ...
40 | step_key: str # ordinal identity, e.g. "webclick#1"
41 | selector_type: Optional[str] = None # CssSelector | XPath
42 | selector_value: Optional[str] = None # e.g. "#btn-login"
43 | args: dict = field(default_factory=dict)
44 | raw_line: str = ""
45 |
46 | @property
47 | def has_selector(self) -> bool:
48 | """True when this step addresses a page element."""
49 | return bool(self.selector_value)
50 |
51 |
52 | def _arg(line: str, name: str) -> Optional[str]:
53 | """Read a --name argument, quoted or bare."""
54 | quoted = re.search(rf'--{name}\s+"([^"]*)"', line, re.IGNORECASE)
55 | if quoted:
56 | return quoted.group(1)
57 | bare = re.search(rf'--{name}\s+([^\s"]+)', line, re.IGNORECASE)
58 | return bare.group(1) if bare else None
59 |
60 |
61 | def parse_wal(wal_path: str) -> list[WalStep]:
62 | """
63 | Parse a .wal file into ordered executable steps.
64 |
65 | Args:
66 | wal_path: Path to the .wal file.
67 |
68 | Returns:
69 | List of WalStep, in file order.
70 | """
71 | steps: list[WalStep] = []
72 | counters: dict[str, int] = {}
73 |
74 | with open(wal_path, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore") as handle:
75 | lines = handle.readlines()
76 |
77 | for line_number, raw_line in enumerate(lines, start=1):
78 | line = raw_line.strip().lstrip("﻿\x00 ")
79 | if not line or line.startswith("//"):

130 | def patch_wal(
131 | wal_path: str,
132 | line_number: int,
133 | old_selector: str,
134 | new_selector: str,
135 | out_path: Optional[str] = None,
136 | ) -> str:
137 | """
138 | Write a patched COPY of a .wal file. The original is never modified.
139 |
140 | Patches ALL lines that reference old_selector, not just the failing line.
141 | This handles the common pattern where webWaitElement and webClick share the
142 | same selector on consecutive lines — both must be updated together.
143 |
144 | Args:
145 | wal_path: Path to the original .wal file.
146 | line_number: 1-based line where the failure was detected (used for
147 | validation — at least this line must be patched).
148 | old_selector: Selector value to replace everywhere in the file.
149 | new_selector: Replacement selector value.
150 | out_path: Destination; defaults to ``<name>.patched.wal``.
151 |
152 | Returns:
153 | Path to the patched copy.
154 | """
155 | with open(wal_path, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore") as handle:
156 | lines = handle.readlines()
157 |
158 | index = line_number - 1
159 | if index < 0 or index >= len(lines):
160 | raise ValueError(
161 | f"Line {line_number} out of range (file has {len(lines)} lines)"
162 | )
163 |
164 | # Patch every line that contains the broken selector
165 | patched_lines = []
166 | patched_count = 0
167 | for i, line in enumerate(lines):
168 | new_line = line.replace(f'"{old_selector}"', f'"{new_selector}"')
169 | if new_line == line:
170 | new_line = line.replace(old_selector, new_selector)
171 | if new_line != line:
172 | patched_count += 1
173 | patched_lines.append(new_line)
174 |
175 | if patched_count == 0:
176 | raise ValueError(f"Selector {old_selector!r} not found anywhere in {wal_path}")
177 |
178 | if out_path is None:
179 | base, ext = os.path.splitext(wal_path)
180 | out_path = base + ".patched" + ext
181 |
182 | with open(out_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
183 | handle.writelines(patched_lines)
184 |
185 | return out_path
186 |
187 |
188 | def diff_wal(original_path: str, patched_path: str) -> list[dict]:
189 | """
190 | Compare two .wal files line by line.
191 |
192 | Returns:
193 | List of ``{line_number, original, patched}`` for each changed line.
194 | """
195 | with open(original_path, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore") as handle:
196 | original_lines = handle.readlines()
197 | with open(patched_path, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore") as handle:
198 | patched_lines = handle.readlines()
199 |
200 | diffs = []
201 | for line_number, (before, after) in enumerate(
202 | zip(original_lines, patched_lines), start=1
203 | ):
204 | if before != after:
205 | diffs.append({
206 | "line_number": line_number,
207 | "original": before.rstrip("\n").strip("\x00"),
208 | "patched": after.rstrip("\n").strip("\x00"),
209 | })
210 | return diffs

3 |
4 | The ranking is plain deterministic code. Most breaks are a renamed id: text,
5 | class, DOM path, position and element type all stay put, the top candidate
6 | scores around 0.9, and no model is called at all.
7 |
8 | score >= 0.85 confident deterministic fix
9 | 0.55 .. 0.85 ambiguous — ask Bob, with the fingerprint, the top three
10 | candidates, and their surrounding context
11 | score < 0.55 escalate to a human; never invent an answer
12 |
13 | Signal weights are frozen with the rest of the contracts.
14 | """

20 | import subprocess
21 | import tempfile
22 | from typing import Optional
23 |
24 | from contracts import AMBIGUOUS_THRESHOLD, CONFIDENT_THRESHOLD
25 |
26 | WEIGHTS = {
27 | "text": 0.30,
28 | "attrs": 0.25,
29 | "dom_path": 0.20,
30 | "geometry": 0.15,
31 | "tag": 0.10,
32 | }
33 |
34 | # Attributes compared for overlap. `id` is one voice among several rather than
35 | # the deciding one: a renamed id costs a candidate roughly 0.08, which leaves a
36 | # plain rename comfortably above the confident threshold while still showing in
37 | # the number. Everything else here survives a routine UI release.
38 | COMPARED_ATTRS = ("id", "class", "type", "name", "aria-label", "placeholder", "role")
39 |
40 | BOB_COMMAND = os.environ.get("BOBMADAK_BOB_CMD", "bob")
41 | BOB_TIMEOUT_SEC = int(os.environ.get("BOBMADAK_BOB_TIMEOUT", "90"))
42 | BOB_ENABLED = os.environ.get("BOBMADAK_BOB_DISABLED", "").lower() not in ("1", "true", "yes")
43 |
44 |
45 | # ── Individual signals ────────────────────────────────────────────
46 |
47 | def _text_score(before: str, after: str) -> float:
48 | """Visible text similarity."""
49 | before = (before or "").strip().lower()
50 | after = (after or "").strip().lower()
51 |
52 | if not before and not after:
53 | return 0.5 # two unlabelled inputs: neutral, not evidence
54 | if not before or not after:
55 | return 0.0
56 | if before == after:
57 | return 1.0
58 | if before in after or after in before:
59 | return 0.75
60 | return round(difflib.SequenceMatcher(None, before, after).ratio(), 4)
61 |
62 |
63 | def _class_overlap(before: str, after: str) -> float:
64 | """Jaccard overlap of two class attribute strings."""
65 | first = set((before or "").split())
66 | second = set((after or "").split())
67 | if not first and not second:
68 | return 1.0
69 | if not first or not second:
70 | return 0.0
71 | return len(first & second) / len(first | second)
72 |
73 |
74 | def _attr_score(before: dict, after: dict) -> float:
75 | """
76 | Overlap of the stable attributes.
77 |
78 | Each attribute present on either side contributes; class is compared as a
79 | set so a single added utility class does not wipe the signal out.
80 | """
81 | total = 0.0
82 | counted = 0
83 |
84 | for name in COMPARED_ATTRS:
85 | left = before.get(name)
86 | right = after.get(name)
87 | if left is None and right is None:
88 | continue
89 | counted += 1
90 | if left is None or right is None:
91 | continue
92 | if name == "class":
93 | total += _class_overlap(left, right)
94 | elif left.strip().lower() == right.strip().lower():
95 | total += 1.0
96 |
97 | if counted == 0:
98 | return 0.5
99 | return round(total / counted, 4)
100 |
101 |
102 | def _dom_path_score(before: str, after: str) -> float:
103 | """Similarity of the two DOM paths, segment by segment."""
104 | if not before or not after:
105 | return 0.0
106 | left = before.lower().split(" > ")
107 | right = after.lower().split(" > ")
108 | ratio = difflib.SequenceMatcher(None, left, right).ratio()
109 |
110 | # The leaf carries the most meaning: reward an exact leaf match.
111 | if left[-1] == right[-1]:
112 | ratio = max(ratio, 0.85)
113 | return round(ratio, 4)
114 |
115 |
116 | def _geometry_score(before: dict, after: dict) -> float:
117 | """Proximity in page position, softened by a size comparison."""
118 | if not before or not after:
119 | return 0.5
120 |
121 | dx = before.get("x", 0) - after.get("x", 0)
122 | dy = before.get("y", 0) - after.get("y", 0)
123 | distance = (dx ** 2 + dy ** 2) ** 0.5
124 |
125 | if distance < 25:
126 | position = 1.0
127 | elif distance < 90:
128 | position = 0.75
129 | elif distance < 250:
130 | position = 0.45
131 | elif distance < 600:
132 | position = 0.2
133 | else:
134 | position = 0.05
135 |
136 | width_before = max(before.get("w", 0), 1)
137 | width_after = max(after.get("w", 0), 1)
138 | height_before = max(before.get("h", 0), 1)
139 | height_after = max(after.get("h", 0), 1)
140 | size = (
141 | min(width_before, width_after) / max(width_before, width_after)
142 | + min(height_before, height_after) / max(height_before, height_after)
143 | ) / 2
144 |
145 | return round(position * 0.75 + size * 0.25, 4)
146 |
147 |
148 | def _tag_score(before: str, after: str) -> float:
149 | """Element type match."""
150 | if not before or not after:
151 | return 0.5
152 | return 1.0 if before.lower() == after.lower() else 0.0
153 |
154 |
155 | def score_candidate(fingerprint: dict, candidate: dict) -> dict:
156 | """
157 | Score one candidate against the fingerprint.
158 |
159 | Returns:
160 | ``{"score": float, "signals": {signal: value}}`` — the per-signal
161 | breakdown is kept so the dashboard can explain the number.
162 | """
163 | signals = {
164 | "text": _text_score(fingerprint.get("text"), candidate.get("text")),
165 | "attrs": _attr_score(fingerprint.get("attrs", {}), candidate.get("attrs", {})),
166 | "dom_path": _dom_path_score(fingerprint.get("dom_path"), candidate.get("dom_path")),
167 | "geometry": _geometry_score(fingerprint.get("geometry", {}), candidate.get("geometry", {})),
168 | "tag": _tag_score(fingerprint.get("tag"), candidate.get("tag")),
169 | }
170 | total = sum(signals[name] * WEIGHTS[name] for name in WEIGHTS)
171 | return {"score": round(total, 4), "signals": signals}
172 |
173 |
174 | def rank_candidates(fingerprint: dict, candidates: list[dict]) -> list[dict]:
175 | """Score every candidate and return them best first."""
176 | ranked = []
177 | for candidate in candidates:
178 | scored = score_candidate(fingerprint, candidate)
179 | ranked.append({**candidate, **scored})
180 | ranked.sort(key=lambda item: item["score"], reverse=True)
181 | return ranked
182 |
183 |
184 | # ── Selector proposals ────────────────────────────────────────────
185 |
186 | def _quote(value: str) -> str:
187 | """Quote a value for a CSS attribute or :has-text() selector."""
188 | return value.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace("'", "\\'")
189 |
190 |
191 | def selector_options(candidate: dict) -> list[dict]:
192 | """
193 | Build replacement selectors for a candidate, most stable first.
194 |
195 | Priority order:
196 | 1. data-testid — the app's own stable hook
197 | 2. new id — standard CSS, works in IBM RPA Studio directly
198 | 3. name attr — stable form field selector
199 | 4. aria-label — accessible label
200 | 5. class — weaker, markup-dependent
201 | 6. has-text — Playwright-only, not supported by IBM RPA Studio
202 |
203 | The new id is promoted above has-text so the patched .wal remains
204 | runnable in IBM RPA Studio without manual editing.
205 | """
206 | tag = candidate.get("tag", "*")
207 | attrs = candidate.get("attrs", {})
208 | text = (candidate.get("text") or "").strip()
209 | element_type = attrs.get("type")
210 | options: list[dict] = []
211 |
212 | testid = attrs.get("data-testid")
213 | if testid:
214 | options.append({
215 | "selector": f"[data-testid='{_quote(testid)}']",
216 | "basis": "data-testid attribute — the application's own stable hook",
217 | })
218 |
219 | # New id first — standard CSS that runs in IBM RPA Studio
220 | element_id = attrs.get("id")
221 | if element_id:
222 | options.append({
223 | "selector": f"#{element_id}",
224 | "basis": "new element id — standard CSS selector",
225 | })
226 |
227 | name = attrs.get("name")
228 | if name:
229 | type_part = f"[type='{_quote(element_type)}']" if element_type else ""
230 | options.append({
231 | "selector": f"{tag}[name='{_quote(name)}']{type_part}",
232 | "basis": "form field name — stable across markup refactors",
233 | })
234 |
235 | aria = attrs.get("aria-label")
236 | if aria:
237 | options.append({
238 | "selector": f"{tag}[aria-label='{_quote(aria)}']",
239 | "basis": "accessible label — tied to meaning, not markup",
240 | })
241 |
242 | classes = [part for part in (attrs.get("class") or "").split() if part]
243 | if classes:
244 | options.append({
245 | "selector": tag + "".join(f".{part}" for part in classes[:2]),
246 | "basis": "element type plus class — weaker, but not id-bound",
247 | })
248 |
249 | # has-text last — Playwright-only, not supported by IBM RPA Studio
250 | if text and tag in ("button", "a"):
251 | base = f"{tag}[type='{_quote(element_type)}']" if element_type else tag
252 | options.append({
253 | "selector": f"{base}:has-text('{_quote(text)}')",
254 | "basis": "visible text plus element type — Playwright only",
255 | })
256 |
257 | return options
258 |
259 |
260 | # ── Bob Shell (the only model call in the system) ─────────────────
261 |
262 | def _build_bob_prompt(fingerprint: dict, top_candidates: list[dict], context_html: str) -> str:
263 | """Compose the disambiguation prompt sent to Bob Shell."""
264 | fingerprint_json = json.dumps(
265 | {key: fingerprint.get(key) for key in
266 | ("step_id", "tag", "text", "attrs", "dom_path", "neighbors", "geometry")},
267 | indent=2, ensure_ascii=False,
268 | )
269 |
270 | blocks = []
271 | for index, candidate in enumerate(top_candidates[:3]):
272 | summary = {key: candidate.get(key) for key in
273 | ("tag", "text", "attrs", "dom_path", "neighbors", "geometry", "score", "signals")}
274 | blocks.append(
275 | f"Candidate {index}:\n{json.dumps(summary, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)}"
276 | )
277 |
278 | return f"""You are the semantic disambiguation step of BotMedic, a self-healing RPA engine.
279 |
280 | An RPA bot failed because the element it used to click no longer matches its selector.
281 | Deterministic scoring (text, attributes, DOM path, geometry, element type) put the best
282 | candidate between {AMBIGUOUS_THRESHOLD} and {CONFIDENT_THRESHOLD}, so the decision needs
283 | semantic judgement: the element's wording may have changed while its purpose did not.
284 |
285 | ORIGINAL ELEMENT, fingerprinted during the last successful run:
286 | {fingerprint_json}
287 |
288 | CANDIDATES on the page as it is now:
289 | {chr(10).join(blocks)}
290 |
291 | SURROUNDING PAGE MARKUP:
292 | {context_html[:4000]}
293 |
294 | Decide which candidate performs the same user-facing action as the original element.
295 | If none of them does, say so — a wrong patch on a live bot is worse than no patch.
296 |
297 | Reply with this JSON object and nothing else:
298 | {{
299 | "selected_candidate_index": <0, 1, 2, or -1 for no valid match>,
300 | "confidence": <float between 0.0 and 1.0>,
301 | "reasoning": "<one sentence, plain English>",
302 | "risk_note": <string or null>
303 | }}"""
304 |
305 |
306 | def ask_bob(fingerprint: dict, top_candidates: list[dict], context_html: str = "") -> dict:
307 | """
308 | Invoke Bob Shell for the ambiguous band and parse its structured answer.
309 |
310 | Any failure — Bob missing, timeout, unparsable output — resolves to "no
311 | match" rather than a guess.
312 | """
313 | if not BOB_ENABLED:
314 | return {
315 | "selected_candidate_index": -1,
316 | "confidence": 0.0,
317 | "reasoning": "Bob calls disabled by BOBMADAK_BOB_DISABLED.",
318 | "risk_note": "Deterministic scoring only.",
319 | "available": False,
320 | }
321 |
322 | prompt = _build_bob_prompt(fingerprint, top_candidates, context_html)
323 | with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(
324 | mode="w", suffix=".txt", delete=False, encoding="utf-8"
325 | ) as handle:
326 | handle.write(prompt)
327 | prompt_path = handle.name
328 |
329 | try:
330 | completed = subprocess.run(
331 | [BOB_COMMAND, "-p", f"@{prompt_path}", "--hide-intermediary-output"],
332 | capture_output=True,
333 | text=True,
334 | timeout=BOB_TIMEOUT_SEC,
335 | encoding="utf-8",
336 | errors="replace",
337 | )
338 | output = (completed.stdout or "").strip()
339 | match = re.search(r"\{[\s\S]*\"selected_candidate_index\"[\s\S]*?\}", output)
340 | payload = json.loads(match.group() if match else output)
341 | payload["available"] = True
342 | return payload
343 | except FileNotFoundError:
344 | return {
345 | "selected_candidate_index": -1,
346 | "confidence": 0.0,
347 | "reasoning": f"Bob Shell executable '{BOB_COMMAND}' not found on PATH.",
348 | "risk_note": "Escalated to a human instead of guessing.",
349 | "available": False,
350 | }
351 | except Exception as error: # noqa: BLE001
352 | return {
353 | "selected_candidate_index": -1,
354 | "confidence": 0.0,
355 | "reasoning": f"Bob Shell call failed: {error}",
356 | "risk_note": "Escalated to a human instead of guessing.",
357 | "available": False,
358 | }
359 | finally:
360 | try:
361 | os.unlink(prompt_path)
362 | except OSError:
363 | pass
364 |
365 |
366 | # ── Diagnosis ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
367 |
368 | def diagnose(
369 | broken_selector: str,
370 | fingerprint: dict,
371 | candidates: list[dict],
372 | context_html: str = "",
373 | ) -> dict:
374 | """
375 | Decide what the broken selector should point at now.
376 |
377 | Args:
378 | broken_selector: Selector that failed.
379 | fingerprint: Fingerprint recorded on the last green run.
380 | candidates: Every interactive element on the page as it is now.
381 | context_html: Markup handed to Bob in the ambiguous band.
382 |
383 | Returns:
384 | {
385 | "broken_selector", "match", "confidence", "resolved_by",
386 | "band", "diagnosis", "ranked", "bob_response"
387 | }
388 |
389 | ``resolved_by`` is None when nothing was resolved.
390 | """
391 | ranked = rank_candidates(fingerprint, candidates)
392 | top = ranked[:3]
393 |
394 | if not top:
395 | return {
396 | "broken_selector": broken_selector,
397 | "match": None,
398 | "confidence": 0.0,
399 | "resolved_by": None,
400 | "band": "no_candidates",
401 | "diagnosis": "No interactive elements found on the page to compare against.",
402 | "ranked": [],
403 | "bob_response": None,
404 | }
405 |
406 | best = top[0]
407 | score = best["score"]
408 |
409 | if score >= CONFIDENT_THRESHOLD:
410 | return {
411 | "broken_selector": broken_selector,
412 | "match": best,
413 | "confidence": score,
414 | "resolved_by": "deterministic",
415 | "band": "confident",
416 | "diagnosis": _explain(fingerprint, best),
417 | "ranked": ranked[:5],
418 | "bob_response": None,
419 | }
420 |
421 | if score >= AMBIGUOUS_THRESHOLD:
422 | bob_response = ask_bob(fingerprint, top, context_html)
423 | index = bob_response.get("selected_candidate_index", -1)
424 | if isinstance(index, int) and 0 <= index < len(top):
425 | chosen = top[index]
426 | confidence = float(bob_response.get("confidence") or score)
427 | return {
428 | "broken_selector": broken_selector,
429 | "match": chosen,
430 | "confidence": round(confidence, 4),
431 | "resolved_by": "bob",
432 | "band": "ambiguous",
433 | "diagnosis": bob_response.get("reasoning")
434 | or _explain(fingerprint, chosen),
435 | "ranked": ranked[:5],
436 | "bob_response": bob_response,
437 | }
438 |
439 | return {
440 | "broken_selector": broken_selector,
441 | "match": None,
442 | "confidence": round(score, 4),
443 | "resolved_by": None,
444 | "band": "ambiguous",
445 | "diagnosis": "Scoring was ambiguous and Bob declined to pick a candidate: "
446 | + str(bob_response.get("reasoning", "no reason given")),
447 | "ranked": ranked[:5],
448 | "bob_response": bob_response,
449 | }
450 |
451 | return {
452 | "broken_selector": broken_selector,
453 | "match": None,
454 | "confidence": round(score, 4),
455 | "resolved_by": None,
456 | "band": "escalate",
457 | "diagnosis": f"Best candidate scored {score:.2f}, below the {AMBIGUOUS_THRESHOLD} "
458 | "floor. No replacement is proposed.",
459 | "ranked": ranked[:5],
460 | "bob_response": None,
461 | }
462 |
463 |
464 | def _explain(fingerprint: dict, candidate: dict) -> str:
465 | """Plain-English account of what changed, built from the signal breakdown."""
466 | signals = candidate.get("signals", {})
467 | before_attrs = fingerprint.get("attrs", {})
468 | after_attrs = candidate.get("attrs", {})
469 |
470 | changed = []
471 | if before_attrs.get("id") != after_attrs.get("id"):
472 | changed.append(
473 | f"id changed from '{before_attrs.get('id', '—')}' to '{after_attrs.get('id', '—')}'"
474 | )
475 | if signals.get("text", 0) < 0.99:
476 | changed.append(
477 | f"visible text changed from '{fingerprint.get('text')}' to '{candidate.get('text')}'"
478 | )
479 | if signals.get("dom_path", 0) < 0.85:
480 | changed.append("the element moved to a different container")
481 | if signals.get("attrs", 0) < 0.8:
482 | changed.append("attributes were refactored")
483 |
484 | stable = [name for name, value in signals.items() if value >= 0.85]
485 | stable_text = ", ".join(stable) if stable else "no signal"
486 |
487 | if not changed:
488 | changed.append("the selector no longer resolves, though every recorded signal matches")
489 |
490 | return f"{'; '.join(changed).capitalize()}. Stable signals: {stable_text}."
491 |
492 |

Contents of file botmedic/src/serve.py:

1 | """
2 | serve.py — static file server for the demo target site.
3 |
4 | Break state is stored server-side in target-site/break-state.json so that
5 | every browser — including the isolated Chrome instance IBM RPA Studio opens —
6 | sees the same DOM mutations without needing shared localStorage.
7 |
8 | The server intercepts requests for index.html and invoices.html, reads the
9 | current break flags, and injects a small inline script that sets localStorage
10 | before the page's own script runs. The page JS reads localStorage as before,
11 | so no page code needed to change.
12 | """
13 |
14 | import json
15 | import socket
16 | import threading
17 | from functools import partial
18 | from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer
19 | from pathlib import Path
20 |
21 | PROJECT_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
22 | SITE_DIR = PROJECT_ROOT / "target-site"
23 | STATE_FILE = SITE_DIR / "break-state.json"
24 |
25 | DEFAULT_HOST = "127.0.0.1"
26 | DEFAULT_PORT = 8000
27 |
28 | _server = None
29 |
30 | BREAK_KEYS = (
31 | "break_login_id",
32 | "break_login_move",
33 | "break_login_text",
34 | "break_export_id",
35 | )
36 |
37 |
38 | def read_break_state() -> dict:
39 | """Return the current break flags from disk (all False when file absent)."""
40 | try:
41 | return json.loads(STATE_FILE.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
42 | except (FileNotFoundError, json.JSONDecodeError):
43 | return {k: False for k in BREAK_KEYS}
44 |
45 |
46 | def write_break_state(flags: dict) -> None:
47 | """Persist break flags to disk."""
48 | STATE_FILE.write_text(
49 | json.dumps({k: bool(flags.get(k, False)) for k in BREAK_KEYS}, indent=2),
50 | encoding="utf-8",
51 | )
52 |
53 |
54 | def _inject_script(html: str, flags: dict) -> bytes:
55 | """
56 | Prepend a localStorage-init script to the page so every browser session
57 | starts with the correct break state, regardless of its own storage.
58 | """
59 | sets = "".join(
60 | f"localStorage.setItem({json.dumps(k)},{json.dumps('true' if flags.get(k) else 'false')});"

## المشكلة

الـ `.wal` الحالي اللي بتشوفه في Studio **هو النسخة المُعالجة (healed)** — لأن الـ heal اشتغل وعدّل الملف لـ `#auth-submit-v2`. لكن `demo-reset.py` بيكتب الملف بـ Python encoding مش نفس الـ encoding بتاع IBM RPA Studio.

المشكلة الحقيقية: **IBM RPA Studio بيكتب الـ .wal بـ UTF-16 LE BOM** وده ظاهر في السطر الأول `\ufffd` (BOM). لما `demo-reset.py` بيكتب الملف بـ `utf-8` مش `utf-16-le`، الملف اللي Studio بيشوفه بيبقى مختلف تماماً.

الآن فاهم البنية تماماً. الـ `.wal` هو:
- **Byte 0:** `0x12` (magic byte ثابت)
- **Bytes 1-2:** varint يحمل طول المحتوى
- **باقي الملف:** نص UTF-8 عادي

المشكلة: لما `demo-reset.py` بيكتب الـ WAL بـ `write_text(encoding='utf-8')` بيكتبه كـ plain text مفيهوش الـ header — فـ IBM RPA Studio مش بيعرف يفتحه. وعشان كده بعد heal الملف بيبقى له header صح لأن `patcher.py` بيقرأ ويكتب binary.

**الحل:** نحدّث `demo-reset.py` و `parser.py` يتعاملوا مع الـ IBM RPA binary format صح — نحتفظ بالـ header الأصلي ونكتب بس المحتوى النصي.

بس الأهم دلوقتي: نحتفظ بـ **backup من الـ bak** الأصلي (اللي IBM RPA Studio كتبه) ونرجعه كاملاً بدل ما نكتب ملف جديد.

bare = re.search(rf'--{name}\s+([^\s"]+)', line, re.IGNORECASE)
return bare.group(1) if bare else None


+def _read_wal_lines(wal_path: str) -> tuple[bytes, list[str]]:
+ """
+ Read an IBM RPA .wal file.
+
+ IBM RPA Studio writes .wal files as:
+ 0x12 <varint: content length> <UTF-8 content>
+
+ Returns:
+ (header_bytes, lines) where header_bytes is the raw prefix that must
+ be preserved when writing back, and lines is the text content split
+ into lines (with line endings).
+ """
+ with open(wal_path, "rb") as fh:
+ raw = fh.read()
+
+ # Detect IBM RPA binary format: magic byte 0x12 followed by a varint length
+ if raw and raw[0] == 0x12:
+ pos = 1
+ result = 0
+ shift = 0
+ while pos < len(raw):
+ b = raw[pos]; pos += 1
+ result |= (b & 0x7f) << shift
+ if not (b & 0x80):
+ break
+ shift += 7
+ header = raw[:pos]
+ content = raw[pos:].decode("utf-8", errors="ignore")
+ else:
+ # Plain-text .wal (e.g. written by older patcher or test fixtures)
+ header = b""
+ content = raw.decode("utf-8", errors="ignore")
+
+ lines = content.splitlines(keepends=True)
+ # splitlines drops a trailing newline — restore it if the content ended with one
+ if content and content[-1] in ("\n", "\r"):
+ lines.append("")
+ return header, lines
+
+
+def _encode_varint(n: int) -> bytes:
+ """Encode a non-negative integer as a protobuf-style varint."""
+ out = []
+ while True:
+ b = n & 0x7f
+ n >>= 7
+ if n:
+ out.append(b | 0x80)
+ else:
+ out.append(b)
+ break
+ return bytes(out)
+
+
+def _write_wal(out_path: str, header: bytes, lines: list[str]) -> None:
+ """Write lines back to a .wal file, re-encoding the length varint."""
+ content_bytes = "".join(lines).encode("utf-8")
+ if header:
+ # header[0] == 0x12 (magic), rest is the old varint — rebuild with new length
+ new_header = bytes([0x12]) + _encode_varint(len(content_bytes))
+ raw = new_header + content_bytes
+ else:
+ raw = content_bytes
+ with open(out_path, "wb") as fh:
+ fh.write(raw)
+
+

## ملخص المشكلة والحل

### المشكلة الجذرية
IBM RPA Studio بيكتب الـ `.wal` بـ **binary format خاص**:

[0x12] [varint: طول المحتوى] [UTF-8 content]


لما `demo-reset.py` القديم كان بيكتب الملف بـ `write_text(encoding='utf-8')` — كان بيكتب plain text **من غير الـ header** ده. Studio مكانش يعرف يفتحه صح.

### اللي اتعمل

| الملف | التعديل |
|---|---|
| [`BobMedic.original.wal`](botmedic/BobMedic.original.wal) | **جديد** — golden master binary، نسخة من الملف الصح |
| [`demo-reset.py`](botmedic/demo-reset.py) | بيستخدم `shutil.copy2` لاستعادة الـ binary مش كتابة text |
| [`src/parser.py`](botmedic/src/parser.py) | `_read_wal_lines()` + `_write_wal()` — يقرأ ويكتب binary format صح |

### النتيجة
- `BobMedic.wal` بعد الـ heal = IBM RPA binary (`0x12` header) ✅
- `BobMedic.wal` بعد `demo-reset.py` = نفس البنية تماماً ✅
- Studio هيشوف الملف صح في الحالتين ✅

1 | """
2 | start.py — one command to bring the whole demo up.
3 |
4 | Starts three things and leaves them running until Ctrl+C:
5 |
6 | target site http://127.0.0.1:8000 the NovaCorp portal the bots drive
7 | control API http://127.0.0.1:8100 incidents, approvals, demo runs
8 | dashboard http://127.0.0.1:3000 the control centre
9 |
10 | The dashboard is optional: if npm is missing, the first two still come up and
11 | the dashboard can be opened later, or read from its built files.
12 | """
13 |
14 | import shutil
15 | import subprocess
16 | import sys
17 | import threading
18 | import time
19 | from pathlib import Path
20 |
21 | PROJECT_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
22 | sys.path.insert(0, str(PROJECT_ROOT / "src"))
23 |
24 | import engine # noqa: E402 - after sys.path setup
25 | from api import API_HOST, API_PORT, BotMedicAPI # noqa: E402
26 | from http.server import ThreadingHTTPServer # noqa: E402
27 | from serve import ensure_server # noqa: E402
28 |
29 |
30 | def start_dashboard() -> subprocess.Popen | None:
31 | """Launch the Vite dev server, if npm and its packages are available."""
32 | npm = shutil.which("npm") or shutil.which("npm.cmd")
33 | dashboard_dir = PROJECT_ROOT / "dashboard"
34 |
35 | if not npm:
36 | print("[skip] npm not found — start the dashboard yourself with 'npm run dev'.")
37 | return None
38 | if not (dashboard_dir / "node_modules").exists():
39 | print("[npm ] installing dashboard packages (first run only)...")
40 | subprocess.run([npm, "install"], cwd=dashboard_dir, check=False)
41 |
42 | return subprocess.Popen(
43 | [npm, "run", "dev"],
44 | cwd=dashboard_dir,
45 | stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL,
46 | stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,
47 | )
48 |
49 |
50 | def main() -> int:
51 | """Bring the demo up and hold it there."""
52 | try:
53 | sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8")
54 | except (AttributeError, OSError):
55 | pass
56 |
57 | site_url = ensure_server()
58 | engine.publish_feed()
59 |
60 | api_server = ThreadingHTTPServer((API_HOST, API_PORT), BotMedicAPI)
61 | threading.Thread(target=api_server.serve_forever, daemon=True).start()
62 |
63 | dashboard = start_dashboard()
64 | time.sleep(1.5)
65 |
66 | print()
67 | print(" Target site " + site_url)
68 | print(" Break panel " + site_url + "/break.html")
69 | print(f" Control API http://{API_HOST}:{API_PORT}/api/feed")
70 | print(" Dashboard http://127.0.0.1:3000" if dashboard else
71 | " Dashboard not started")
72 | print()
73 | print(" Break a bot from the dashboard, or from the command line:")
74 | print(" python src/engine.py demo invoice-extract rename-login-id")
75 | print()
76 | print(" Ctrl+C to stop.")
77 |
78 | try:
79 | while True:
80 | time.sleep(1)
81 | except KeyboardInterrupt:
82 | print("\nStopping...")
83 | finally:
84 | api_server.shutdown()
85 | if dashboard:
86 | dashboard.terminate()
87 | return 0
88 |
89 |
90 | if __name__ == "__main__":
91 | sys.exit(main())

## تلخيص المشكلتين واللي اتعمل

### المشكلة 1 — `ConnectionAbortedError` tracebacks

**السبب:** لما IBM RPA Studio browser يفتح صفحة وبعدين يقفلها قبل ما الـ response ينتهي — Windows بيبعت `WinError 10053`. ده **طبيعي تماماً** ومش بيأثر على أي حاجة.

**الحل في [`serve.py`](botmedic/src/serve.py):**
- أضفنا `log_error()` يـ suppress الـ tracebacks
- لففنا `wfile.write(body)` بـ `try/except` على الـ connection errors الثلاث الشائعة في Windows

### المشكلة 2 — الـ break state مش reset

**السبب:** `break-state.json` كان فيه `break_login_id: true` + `break_export_id: true` من تشغيل سابق.

**الحل:** `python demo-reset.py` — أمسحها وسجّل baseline جديد.

لو عايز تعمل نفس الحاجة يدوياً في أي وقت، الأمر ده:

powershell
@(8000, 8100, 3000) | ForEach-Object {
    $port = $_
    $pids = netstat -ano | Select-String ":$port\s" | ForEach-Object {
        ($_ -split '\s+')[-1]
    } | Sort-Object -Unique
    foreach ($p in $pids) {
        if ($p -match '^\d+$' -and $p -ne '0') {
            Stop-Process -Id $p -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
            Write-Host "Killed PID $p on port $port"
        }
    }
}

166 | """Map a Playwright failure onto the error vocabulary the dashboard shows."""
167 | message = str(error).lower()
168 | if "timeout" in message and "waiting for" in message:
169 | return "ElementNotFound"

1 | """
2 | parser.py — WAL script reader and patch writer for BotMedic.
3 |
4 | Reads an IBM RPA .wal script and returns every executable step with its line
5 | number, so the runner can replay the bot and the patcher can rewrite exactly
6 | one line without touching anything else.
7 |
8 | Step identity
9 | -------------
10 | A step is addressed by an ordinal key such as ``webclick#1`` — the first
11 | ``webClick`` in the file. Ordinals survive a selector patch, which is why they
12 | are used as the fingerprint key instead of the selector itself. The bot
13 | registry maps an ordinal key to a human step id (``login_submit``).
14 | """
15 |
16 | import os
17 | import re
18 | from pathlib import Path
19 | from dataclasses import dataclass, field
20 | from typing import Optional
21 |
22 | # Commands the runner knows how to replay.
23 | WEB_COMMANDS = {
24 | "webstart", "webnavigate", "webset", "webclick", "webget",
25 | "webwait", "webwaitelement", "webassert", "webhover", "webselect", "webclose",
26 | }
27 |
28 | # Commands that address an element and can therefore break.
29 | SELECTOR_COMMANDS = {
30 | "webset", "webclick", "webget", "webwait", "webwaitelement", "webassert",
31 | "webhover", "webselect",
32 | }
33 |
34 |
35 | @dataclass
36 | class WalStep:
37 | """A single executable line of a .wal script."""
38 |
39 | line_number: int
40 | command: str # lowercase: webclick, webset, ...
41 | step_key: str # ordinal identity, e.g. "webclick#1"
42 | selector_type: Optional[str] = None # CssSelector | XPath
43 | selector_value: Optional[str] = None # e.g. "#btn-login"
44 | args: dict = field(default_factory=dict)
45 | raw_line: str = ""
46 |
47 | @property
48 | def has_selector(self) -> bool:
49 | """True when this step addresses a page element."""
50 | return bool(self.selector_value)
51 |
52 |
53 | def _arg(line: str, name: str) -> Optional[str]:
54 | """Read a --name argument, quoted or bare."""
55 | quoted = re.search(rf'--{name}\s+"([^"]*)"', line, re.IGNORECASE)
56 | if quoted:
57 | return quoted.group(1)
58 | bare = re.search(rf'--{name}\s+([^\s"]+)', line, re.IGNORECASE)
59 | return bare.group(1) if bare else None
60 |

184 | # ── Selector proposals ────────────────────────────────────────────
185 |
186 | def _quote(value: str) -> str:
187 | """Quote a value for a CSS attribute or :has-text() selector."""
188 | return value.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace("'", "\\'")
189 |
190 |
191 | def _attr_value(value: str) -> str:
192 | """
193 | Render an attribute value for a CSS selector.
194 |
195 | Left unquoted whenever CSS allows it. IBM RPA Studio reads the selector out
196 | of the .wal line, and a quote inside that value throws its parser off: the
197 | line is then reported as an invalid output expression and the script will
198 | not load. Plain identifiers therefore stay bare.
199 | """
200 | if re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z_][\w-]*", value or ""):
201 | return value
202 | return chr(39) + _quote(value) + chr(39)
203 |
204 |
205 | def selector_options(candidate: dict) -> list[dict]:
206 | """
207 | Build replacement selectors for a candidate, most stable first.
208 |
209 | Three constraints shape the order, and all three are real:
210 |
211 | * IBM RPA Studio must be able to load the patched script. It takes ordinary
212 | CSS, has no `:has-text()` (a Playwright extension), and its line parser
213 | is unhappy with quotes inside a selector value — so the plainest form of
214 | a selector is preferred, and quotes are avoided where CSS permits.
215 | * A selector rebuilt from the id that just changed will break again on the
216 | next release, which is the failure being healed.
217 | * Whatever is chosen has to match exactly one element, which the caller
218 | checks against the live page.
219 |
220 | 1. data-testid the app's own stable hook
221 | 2. type + class plainest durable form: no brackets, no quotes
222 | 3. name stable form-field identity
223 | 4. class + type narrows when the class alone is ambiguous
224 | 5. aria-label tied to meaning, but needs quoting
225 | 6. structural an ancestor id from the DOM path plus the leaf
226 | 7. new id last resort in valid CSS
227 | 8. has-text Playwright only; unusable in Studio, so truly last
228 | """
229 | tag = candidate.get("tag", "*")
230 | attrs = candidate.get("attrs", {})
231 | text = (candidate.get("text") or "").strip()
232 | element_type = attrs.get("type")
233 | options: list[dict] = []
234 |
235 | testid = attrs.get("data-testid")
236 | if testid:
237 | options.append({
238 | "selector": f"[data-testid={_attr_value(testid)}]",
239 | "basis": "data-testid attribute — the application's own stable hook",
240 | })
241 |
242 | classes = [part for part in (attrs.get("class") or "").split() if part]
243 | class_part = "".join(f".{part}" for part in classes[:2])
244 |
245 | # Plainest durable selector: nothing in it that a parser can trip over.
246 | if classes:
247 | options.append({
248 | "selector": f"{tag}{class_part}",
249 | "basis": "element type and class — plain CSS, nothing to misparse",
250 | })
251 |
252 | name = attrs.get("name")
253 | if name:
254 | type_part = f"[type={_attr_value(element_type)}]" if element_type else ""
255 | options.append({
256 | "selector": f"{tag}[name={_attr_value(name)}]{type_part}",
257 | "basis": "form field name — stable across markup refactors",
258 | })
259 |
260 | # Same as the class selector, narrowed, for pages where the class repeats.

62 | def _read_wal_lines(wal_path: str) -> tuple[bytes, list[str]]:
63 | """
64 | Read an IBM RPA .wal file.
65 |
66 | IBM RPA Studio writes .wal files as:
67 | 0x12 <varint: content length> <UTF-8 content>
68 |
69 | Returns:
70 | (header_bytes, lines) where header_bytes is the raw prefix that must
71 | be preserved when writing back, and lines is the text content split
72 | into lines (with line endings).
73 | """
74 | with open(wal_path, "rb") as fh:
75 | raw = fh.read()
76 |
77 | # Detect IBM RPA binary format: magic byte 0x12 followed by a varint length
78 | if raw and raw[0] == 0x12:
79 | pos = 1
80 | result = 0
81 | shift = 0
82 | while pos < len(raw):
83 | b = raw[pos]; pos += 1
84 | result |= (b & 0x7f) << shift
85 | if not (b & 0x80):
86 | break
87 | shift += 7
88 | header = raw[:pos]
89 | content = raw[pos:].decode("utf-8", errors="ignore")
90 | else:
91 | # Plain-text .wal (e.g. written by older patcher or test fixtures)
92 | header = b""
93 | content = raw.decode("utf-8", errors="ignore")
94 |
95 | lines = content.splitlines(keepends=True)
96 | # splitlines drops a trailing newline — restore it if the content ended with one
97 | if content and content[-1] in ("\n", "\r"):
98 | lines.append("")
99 | return header, lines
100 |
101 |
102 | def _encode_varint(n: int) -> bytes:
103 | """Encode a non-negative integer as a protobuf-style varint."""
104 | out = []
105 | while True:
106 | b = n & 0x7f
107 | n >>= 7
108 | if n:
109 | out.append(b | 0x80)
110 | else:
111 | out.append(b)
112 | break
113 | return bytes(out)
114 |
115 |
116 | def _write_wal(out_path: str, header: bytes, lines: list[str]) -> None:
117 | """Write lines back to a .wal file, re-encoding the length varint."""
118 | content_bytes = "".join(lines).encode("utf-8")
119 | if header:
120 | # header[0] == 0x12 (magic), rest is the old varint — rebuild with new length
121 | new_header = bytes([0x12]) + _encode_varint(len(content_bytes))
122 | raw = new_header + content_bytes

197 | # ── WAL container format ──────────────────────────────────────────
198 | #
199 | # A .wal saved by IBM RPA Studio is not plain text. It is a small
200 | # protobuf-style container:
201 | #
202 | # 0x12 <varint: body length> <script body> 0x2A 0x09 "23.0.19.0"
203 | #
204 | # Reading it as text and writing it back destroys three things at once: the
205 | # raw header byte becomes U+FFFD, the length prefix stops matching the body,
206 | # and the version trailer is dropped. Studio then refuses the file with
207 | # "Command not found on line 0". Patching therefore happens on bytes, and the
208 | # length prefix is recomputed.
209 |
210 |
211 | def _varint_decode(data: bytes, offset: int) -> tuple[int, int]:
212 | """Decode a varint. Returns (value, bytes consumed)."""
213 | value = shift = consumed = 0
214 | while offset + consumed < len(data):
215 | byte = data[offset + consumed]
216 | value |= (byte & 0x7F) << shift
217 | consumed += 1
218 | if not byte & 0x80:
219 | return value, consumed
220 | shift += 7
221 | raise ValueError("truncated varint in .wal header")
222 |
223 |
224 | def _varint_encode(value: int) -> bytes:
225 | """Encode an integer as a varint."""
226 | out = bytearray()
227 | while True:
228 | byte = value & 0x7F
229 | value >>= 7
230 | out.append(byte | (0x80 if value else 0))
231 | if not value:
232 | return bytes(out)
233 |
234 |
235 | def split_container(raw: bytes) -> tuple[bytes, bytes]:
236 | """
237 | Split a .wal into (script body, trailer).
238 |
239 | A plain-text .wal — one written by hand rather than saved by Studio —
240 | has no container, and is returned unchanged with an empty trailer.
241 | """
242 | if not raw.startswith(bytes((0x12,))):
243 | return raw, b""
244 | try:
245 | length, consumed = _varint_decode(raw, 1)
246 | except ValueError:
247 | return raw, b""
248 |
249 | start = 1 + consumed
250 | end = start + length
251 | if end > len(raw):
252 | # Length prefix disagrees with the file: treat it as plain text rather
253 | # than silently truncating someone's script.
254 | return raw, b""
255 | return raw[start:end], raw[end:]
256 |
257 |
258 | def build_container(body: bytes, trailer: bytes) -> bytes:
259 | """Rebuild a Studio .wal around a modified body, with a correct length."""
260 | if not trailer:
261 | return body
262 | return bytes((0x12,)) + _varint_encode(len(body)) + body + trailer
263 |

330 | """
331 | Replace a selector everywhere it appears in a script, not just where it failed.
332 |
333 | A renamed id breaks every line that referenced it. Patching only the failing
334 | step leaves the next one pointing at the same dead selector, and the
335 | verification re-run then fails a line later — which reads as "no fix found"
336 | when the fix was simply incomplete.
337 |
338 | Args:
339 | wal_path: Path to the original .wal file.
340 | old_selector: Selector value to replace.
341 | new_selector: Replacement selector value.
342 | out_path: Destination; defaults to ``<name>.patched.wal``.

345 | ``(path to the patched copy, line numbers changed)``.

348 | step.line_number
349 | for step in parse_wal(wal_path)
350 | if step.selector_value == old_selector
351 | ]

363 | new_bytes = new_selector.encode("utf-8")
364 | quoted_old = bytes((34,)) + old_bytes + bytes((34,))
365 | quoted_new = bytes((34,)) + new_bytes + bytes((34,))
366 |
367 | changed = []

369 | index = line_number - 1
370 | if index < 0 or index >= len(lines):
371 | continue
372 | original_line = lines[index]
373 | patched_line = original_line.replace(quoted_old, quoted_new)
374 | if patched_line == original_line:

376 | if patched_line != original_line:

205 | def selector_options(candidate: dict) -> list[dict]:
206 | """
207 | Build replacement selectors for a candidate, most stable first.
208 |
209 | Three constraints shape the order, and all three are real:
210 |
211 | * IBM RPA Studio must be able to load the patched script. It takes ordinary
212 | CSS, has no `:has-text()` (a Playwright extension), and its line parser
213 | is unhappy with quotes inside a selector value — so the plainest form of
214 | a selector is preferred, and quotes are avoided where CSS permits.
215 | * A selector rebuilt from the id that just changed will break again on the
216 | next release, which is the failure being healed.
217 | * Whatever is chosen has to match exactly one element, which the caller
218 | checks against the live page.
219 |
220 | 1. data-testid the app's own stable hook
221 | 2. type + class plainest durable form: no brackets, no quotes
222 | 3. name stable form-field identity
223 | 4. class + type narrows when the class alone is ambiguous
224 | 5. aria-label tied to meaning, but needs quoting
225 | 6. structural an ancestor id from the DOM path plus the leaf
226 | 7. new id last resort in valid CSS
227 | 8. has-text Playwright only; unusable in Studio, so truly last
228 | """
229 | tag = candidate.get("tag", "*")
230 | attrs = candidate.get("attrs", {})
231 | text = (candidate.get("text") or "").strip()
232 | element_type = attrs.get("type")
233 | options: list[dict] = []
234 |
235 | testid = attrs.get("data-testid")
236 | if testid:
237 | options.append({
238 | "selector": f"[data-testid={_attr_value(testid)}]",
239 | "basis": "data-testid attribute — the application's own stable hook",
240 | })
241 |
242 | classes = [part for part in (attrs.get("class") or "").split() if part]
243 | class_part = "".join(f".{part}" for part in classes[:2])
244 |
245 | # Plainest durable selector: nothing in it that a parser can trip over.
246 | if classes:
247 | options.append({
248 | "selector": f"{tag}{class_part}",
249 | "basis": "element type and class — plain CSS, nothing to misparse",
250 | })
251 |
252 | name = attrs.get("name")

254 | type_part = f"[type={_attr_value(element_type)}]" if element_type else ""

256 | "selector": f"{tag}[name={_attr_value(name)}]{type_part}",
257 | "basis": "form field name — stable across markup refactors",
258 | })
259 |
260 | # Same as the class selector, narrowed, for pages where the class repeats.
261 | if classes and element_type:

1 | """
2 | parser.py — WAL script reader and patch writer for BotMedic.
3 |
4 | Reads an IBM RPA .wal script and returns every executable step with its line
5 | number, so the runner can replay the bot and the patcher can rewrite exactly
6 | one line without touching anything else.
7 |
8 | Step identity
9 | -------------
10 | A step is addressed by an ordinal key such as ``webclick#1`` — the first
11 | ``webClick`` in the file. Ordinals survive a selector patch, which is why they
12 | are used as the fingerprint key instead of the selector itself. The bot
13 | registry maps an ordinal key to a human step id (``login_submit``).
14 | """
15 |
16 | import os
17 | import re
18 | from pathlib import Path
19 | from dataclasses import dataclass, field
20 | from typing import Optional
21 |
22 | # Commands the runner knows how to replay.
23 | WEB_COMMANDS = {
24 | "webstart", "webnavigate", "webset", "webclick", "webget",
25 | "webwait", "webwaitelement", "webassert", "webhover", "webselect", "webclose",
26 | }
27 |
28 | # Commands that address an element and can therefore break.
29 | SELECTOR_COMMANDS = {
30 | "webset", "webclick", "webget", "webwait", "webwaitelement", "webassert",
31 | "webhover", "webselect",
32 | }
33 |
34 |
35 | @dataclass
36 | class WalStep:
37 | """A single executable line of a .wal script."""
38 |
39 | line_number: int
40 | command: str # lowercase: webclick, webset, ...
41 | step_key: str # ordinal identity, e.g. "webclick#1"
42 | selector_type: Optional[str] = None # CssSelector | XPath
43 | selector_value: Optional[str] = None # e.g. "#btn-login"
44 | args: dict = field(default_factory=dict)
45 | raw_line: str = ""
46 |
47 | @property
48 | def has_selector(self) -> bool:
49 | """True when this step addresses a page element."""
50 | return bool(self.selector_value)

1 | """
2 | serve.py — static file server for the demo target site.
3 |
4 | Break state is stored server-side in target-site/break-state.json so that
5 | every browser — including the isolated Chrome instance IBM RPA Studio opens —
6 | sees the same DOM mutations without needing shared localStorage.
7 |
8 | The server intercepts requests for index.html and invoices.html, reads the
9 | current break flags, and injects a small inline script that sets localStorage
10 | before the page's own script runs. The page JS reads localStorage as before,
11 | so no page code needed to change.
12 | """
13 |
14 | import json
15 | import socket
16 | import time
17 | import threading
18 | from functools import partial
19 | from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer
20 | from pathlib import Path
21 |
22 | PROJECT_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
